a.q: Where does most of Australia's rain fall?
opts: On the north and east coasts
In the centre of the continent
Evenly across the whole continent
Under the ground in the inland

b.clue: The water may not be on the surface.

a.q: Which description best fits where Australia's water is found?
opts: Most rain falls on the north and east coasts
Most rain falls in the centre of the continent
Most rain falls evenly across every region
Most rain falls on the south and west deserts
a.why: The north and east coasts receive the most rain. The centre is the driest part, so it is not where most rain falls.
a.clue: Think about which parts of the map are coastal and wet.

b.q: Ben lives in a dry inland town in Queensland with little rain. Where might a large store of water still be found near him?
opts: In groundwater, such as the Great Artesian Basin
In rivers that carry the heavy rain of the inland every year
In large lakes that fill from regular inland rain each year
In water stored in the air above the inland desert
b.why: Large stores of groundwater lie under the inland, and the Great Artesian Basin lies under parts of Queensland. Regular heavy inland rain is wrong because the inland gets little rain.
b.clue: The water may not be on the surface.

a.best: Most rain falls on the north and east coasts

b.best: In groundwater, such as the Great Artesian Basin

version.title: Where Australia's water is
card: Australia is the driest inhabited continent. Only Antarctica is drier, and no one lives there permanently.
Rain falls most on the north and east coasts. Much of the inland gets little rain, so water on the surface there is scarce.
Groundwater is water stored in the soil and rock under the ground. Large stores of it lie under the inland.
The Great Artesian Basin is one of these stores. It lies under parts of Queensland, South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory.
version.remember: Rain falls most on the north and east coasts, while large stores of groundwater lie under the dry inland.

a.q: Which part of Australia gets the most rain?
opts: The north and east coasts
The middle of the continent
Every part gets about the same
The dry inland plains
a.why: The north and east coasts get the most rain, while much of the inland gets little. Large stores of water do lie under the inland, but that is groundwater, not rain falling there.
a.clue: Much of Australia's centre is very dry.

b.q: Ben lives in a dry town in western Queensland where little rain falls. A visitor asks where a large store of water could be found near the town. What should Ben say?
opts: In groundwater stored in rock under the inland
In a large lake on the surface that stays full
In inland rivers that run high all year round
In a big dam filled by the town's own rainfall
b.why: Large stores of groundwater lie under the inland, and the Great Artesian Basin lies under parts of Queensland. The inland gets little rain, so its surface water is scarce, which rules out a lake that stays full, rivers running high all year or a dam filled by local rain.
b.clue: Little rain means little water stays on the surface.

b.best: In groundwater stored in rock under the inland
